summary.text: Chris Stearns is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives from District 47-Position 2, where he has served since January 2023, and he is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot seeking re-election.
An attorney and former Auburn City Councilmember, he is Speaker Pro Tem of the House.

paragraphs.text: Chris Stearns graduated from The Lawrenceville School in 1982, earned a B.A. with honors in history from Williams College in 1986 and a J.D. from Cornell Law School in 1989.

He is Navajo and, according to the House Democrats' biography, served as Democratic counsel for the U.S. House Committee on Natural Resources and was appointed by President Bill Clinton as the first Director of Native American Affairs at the U.S. Department of Energy.
He served two terms as Chair of the Washington State Gambling Commission and was the first Native American on the Auburn City Council.
Ballotpedia also lists him as a board member and chairman of the Seattle Indian Health Board.
Stearns took office in the House on January 9, 2023, succeeding Pat Sullivan.
He serves on the Rules, Capital Budget, Environment & Energy, and State Government & Tribal Relations committees and chairs the House Members of Color Caucus.

The House Democrats' biography lists his legislative priorities as the state's energy system, the environment, good jobs for working families, small business owners, civil rights and tribal sovereignty.
